items.title: On the hypothesis of psychological barriers in stock markets and Benford's Law
Psychological Barriers in Stocks and Stock Indices - Evidence from European Markets
items.abstract: <jats:p>We examine four European stock indices and the prices of eight major German stocks for indications of psychological barriers. Frequency, (expected) returns, intraday volatility and trading volume of these assets are studied when the prices lie within a certain band around round numbers. We find evidence for the existence of psychological barriers, but the assets behave differently at the barriers. Additionally, the indications for psychological barriers are stronger for indices than for stocks.</jats:p>

items.title: Testing the martingale hypothesis for futures prices: Implications for hedgers
items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>The martingale hypothesis for futures prices is investigated using a nonparametric approach where it is assumed that the expected futures returns depend (nonparametrically) on a linear combination of predictors. We first collapse the predictors into a single‐index variable where the weights are identified up to scale, using the average derivative estimator proposed by T. Stoker (1986).
